title: Temple Warning Inscription
summary: A Greek limestone warning from the Herodian temple complex that prohibited foreigners from crossing the balustrade around the sanctuary under threat of death.
historical_context: The complete stone was found in Jerusalem in 1871 and is held by the Istanbul Archaeology Museums as 2196 T; a fragmentary parallel is held by the Israel Museum. The warning belongs to the Herodian temple horizon before its destruction in 70 CE.
ancient_near_east_context: The operative setting is Roman-period Jerusalem. The inscription is direct evidence for a locally enforced sacred-space boundary and should not be replaced with generic claims about ancient inscriptions or imperial administration.
hebraic_worldview: The warning materializes graded holiness and restricted access within the temple complex while using Greek to address visitors who might not read Hebrew or Aramaic.
second_temple_context: The inscription and Josephus independently describe a boundary separating areas open to foreigners from the more restricted sanctuary precinct.
canonical_context: Acts 21 narrates an accusation that Paul brought a Greek into the temple. The stone explains the institutional seriousness of the alleged boundary crossing without determining whether it occurred.
literary_context: Acts 21:27-36 distinguishes the accusation made by Judeans from Asia, the crowd's response, and Roman intervention. The inscription supplies context for the accusation, not proof of its truth.
covenantal_significance: The artifact witnesses one historical expression of sacred-space access in late Second Temple Judaism; it does not prescribe a timeless ethnic boundary or settle later theological reuse of temple imagery.
original_audience: Greek-reading visitors approaching restricted areas of the Jerusalem temple complex.
historical_setting: Herodian temple complex in Jerusalem, approximately 23 BCE-70 CE.
canonical_role: The inscription is a contemporary material anchor for the restricted temple boundary presupposed by Acts 21, with explicit limits on what it can verify.

related_objects.notes: The warning regulated access inside the Herodian temple complex.
The complete stone was found near the Temple Mount.
Temple authorities and officers maintained access boundaries.

scripture_references.notes: Contemporary context for the restricted boundary central to the accusation against Paul.
Possible conceptual comparison with dividing-wall imagery; direct dependence is not assumed.

interpretive_notes.note: The complete Istanbul stone is not the Tel Dan Stele and contains no House of David reference.
interpretive_notes.rationale: The former record had conflated two unrelated inscriptions.

interpretive_notes.note: The warning independently attests a boundary but cannot establish whether Paul crossed it or whether the crowd's accusation was correct.
interpretive_notes.rationale: Artifact and narrative make different claims.
